questions.answer: 3 feet
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 1786 , § 1, adopted Oct. 7, 2024, set out language stating "The city's building official

               (7), fifteen (15), and nineteen (19) of the ordinances of the Code of the City of
               Goodland, to make such investigations, issue citations, sign complaints, issue notices,
               orders and directions as are necessary for the enforcement of provisions of the ordinances.
               Citations issued under these chapters shall be turned in to the Municipal Court Clerk
               within the next business day or as soon as reasonably possible." Cross reference— Parking and transporting hazardous materials, § 7-1001 et seq.

All sidewalks constructed or reconstructed in this city shall be constructed on the
               established grade, the grade to be so established that there shall be one-fourth inch
               of slope per foot. (Ord. No. 817, § 1)

All sidewalks hereafter constructed or reconstructed must match existing sidewalks
               in each block as to location or abut the curb provided that paved access is provided
               between sidewalks located on adjacent properties. If no sidewalk exists in a block,
               the sidewalk must abut the curb. (Ord. No. 817, § 2; Ord. No. 1397, § 1, 4-6-98)

All sidewalks constructed or reconstructed in any residential zones, as defined by
               the zoning laws of the City of Goodland, shall be a minimum of three feet in width
               by four inches in thickness, and all other sidewalks constructed or reconstructed
               in all other zones according to the zoning laws of the city shall be a minimum of
               four feet in width by four inches in thickness. Any variation must be approved by
               the city building inspector or an agent of same. (Ord. No. 817, § 3)

questions.prompt: Can you bring a firearm or other dangerous weapon into a Lyons city park?
choices: Yes, if you have a license
No, except for on-duty law enforcement officers
Yes, as long as you do not shoot it
questions.answer: No, except for on-duty law enforcement officers
questions.excerpt:
The laws of the city shall extend to and cover all city parks. Police regulations
               shall govern all public parks belonging to the city, and the police chief and law
               enforcement officers of the city shall have full power to enforce city laws governing
               city parks and shall maintain order therein. (Code 2006, §§ 12-101, 12-102)

It is unlawful for any person, except duly authorized city employees, to willfully
               or wantonly injure, tarnish, deface or destroy any building, walk, bench, tree or
               improvement or property of any kind belonging to any park owned by the city. (Code 2006, § 12-103)

It is unlawful for any person to carry or have in his possession any firearm or dangerous
               weapon or to shoot or discharge the same within the limits of any city parks; provided,
               however, that this prohibition shall not apply to duly authorized law enforcement
               officers in the performance of official duty. (Code 2006, § 12-104)

(a) Motor vehicles, including any vehicle licensed to operate on public streets, roads
               and highways, and motorbikes, go-carts, snowmobiles and other motorized off-road vehicles
               shall be operated in a safe and prudent manner at all times in park areas. (b) It is unlawful for any person to park any motor vehicle in any area not designated
               for such purpose or to operate any motor vehicle within any city park, except upon
               roads, drives and parking areas established by the city; provided, however, that this
               section shall not apply to authorized city employees while engaged in the maintenance
               and care of the park. (c) It is unlawful to operate any such vehicle in any park area at a speed in excess of
               20 miles per hour. (Code 2006, § 12-105)

questions.prompt: When selling candy in a Manhattan store, it counts as alcoholic candy if it has more than what alcohol content?
choices: Greater than one-half percent alcohol by volume
Greater than one percent alcohol by volume
More than 3.2 percent alcohol by weight
Any amount of alcohol at all
questions.answer: Greater than one percent alcohol by volume
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Secs. 1—67 of Ord. No. 6958, adopted Aug. 14, 2012, amended ch. 4 in its entirety
               to read as herein set out. See Code Comparative Table for prior amendatory history. Cross reference— Consumption of alcohol at airport, § 7-60; alcoholic liquor prohibited in memorial auditorium, § 23-52. State Law reference— Intoxicating liquors and beverages, K.S.A. Ch. 41

The following words and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall mean: Alcohol means the product of distillation of any fermented liquid, whether rectified or diluted,
               whatever its origin, and includes synthetic ethyl alcohol but does not include denatured
               alcohol or wood alcohol. Alcoholic Beverage Control or ABC means the State of Kansas Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control. ABC director or director means the Director of the State of Kansas Division of Alcohol Beverage Control. Alcoholic candy means (1) For purposes of manufacturing, any candy or other confectionery product with an
               alcohol content greater than one-half percent alcohol by volume; and (2) For purposes of sale at retail, any candy or other confectionery product with
               an alcohol content greater than one percent alcohol by volume. Alcoholic liquor means alcohol, spirits, wine, beer, alcoholic candy and every liquid or solid, patented
               or not, containing alcohol, spirits, wine or beer and capable of being consumed as
               a beverage by a human being, but shall not include any cereal malt beverage. Beer means a beverage, containing more than three and two-tenths percent alcohol by weight,
               obtained by alcoholic fermentation of an infusion or concoction of barley, or other
               grain, malt and hops in water and includes beer, ale, stout, lager beer, porter and
               similar beverages having such alcoholic content. Caterer means an individual, partnership or corporation that sells…

questions.prompt: If an animal stays at your house in Prairie Village for three days in a row, what does city code presume?
choices: You are the person responsible for the animal
The city now owns the animal
You must give it back within 24 hours
Nothing, unless it has a license
questions.answer: You are the person responsible for the animal
questions.excerpt:
The purpose of this chapter is to promote harmonious relationships in the interaction
               between humans and animals by: (a) Protecting animals from improper use, abuse, neglect, exploitation, inhumane treatment
                  and health hazards; (b) Delineating the responsibility of persons for the acts and behavior of such persons'
                  animals at all times; (c) Providing regulations that foster a reduced risk to residents from annoyance, intimidation,
                  injury and health hazards by animals; and (d) Encouraging responsible pet ownership. ( Ord. 2325 , Sec. 1, 2015; Ord. 2368 , Sec. 1, 2017)

(a) Abandon includes the leaving of an animal by the person responsible therefor without making
               effective provisions for its proper care. (b) Adequate care means normal and prudent attention to the needs of an animal, including that care
               which is normally necessary to maintain good health in a specific animal. (c) Adequate food means supplying at suitable intervals (not to exceed 24 hours) of a quantity of food
               suitable and sufficient to maintain a reasonable level of nutrition for each animal. (d) Adequate health care means the provision to each healthy animal of all immunizations and preventative
               care required to maintain good health, space adequate to allow the animal rest and
               exercise sufficient to maintain good health, and the provision to each sick, diseased,
               or injured animal of necessary veterinary care or humane death. (e) Adequate shelter means a structurally sound, properly ventilated, sanitary and weatherproof shelter,
               which provides access to shade from direct sunlight and protection from exposure to
               inclement weather conditions. (f) Adequate water means a continual access to a supply of clean, fresh, potable water provided in a
               sanitary manner. (g) Animal is any living creature, other…

questions.prompt: Before you construct, reconstruct, or even repair a sidewalk in Pratt, what has to happen first?
choices: You post a sign on the property for 10 days
The city must approve the plans and issue a permit
Your neighbors must all sign off
A county inspector marks the lot
questions.answer: The city must approve the plans and issue a permit
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

The city manager or other authorized official may, as hereinafter provided, order
               sidewalks, crosswalks and curbs constructed, reconstructed or replaced on any street,
               avenue or alley or any portion thereof in the city. (Ord. 9101 § 1 (part), 1991: prior code § 13-101)

It is unlawful to construct, reconstruct or repair any sidewalk within the city until
               the plans first have been approved by the governing body and a permit issued for such
               work by the city. (Ord. 9101 § 1 (part), 1991: prior code § 13-102)

Before any sidewalk, crosswalk, or curb shall be laid or constructed, the city manager
               or other duly authorized official shall ascertain and indicate the property line according
               to the recorded plat thereof. He or she shall establish and stake out the alignment
               and grade of such sidewalk and it shall be built and constructed in conformity therewith. (Ord. 9101 § 1 (part), 1991: prior code § 13-103)

Except where otherwise provided, the inner edge of all four-foot walks shall be one
               foot from the lot line, and all four-foot walks shall be of three-fourths inch downward
               slope toward the curb. The top of the inner edge of the sidewalk shall be three inches
               above the grade line and/or three inches above the top of the curbing where curb and
               gutter have previously been laid unless a permit to construct the sidewalk in a different
               manner shall have been issued by the city engineer and approved by the board of commissioners
               of the city; provided, that wherever the curbline and the outer edge of the sidewalk
               are contiguous the outer edge of the sidewalk shall be constructed on a level with
               the curb. (Ord. 9101 § 1 (part), 1991: prior code § 13-104)

Hereafter all sidewalks constructed or reconstructed in the city shall be…

questions.prompt: In Shawnee, leaving an animal without adequate care for more than how long can count as abandoning it?
questions.answer: 12 hours
questions.excerpt:
Chapters

Sections

When the terms set forth in this Chapter are used in this Title, each shall have the
               meaning respectively ascribed in this Chapter. A. Abandon means for the Owner, Keeper or Harborer to leave an Animal without demonstrated or
                  apparent intent to recover or resume custody; to leave an Animal for more than twelve
                  (12) hours without providing Adequate Care for the duration of the absence; to turn
                  out or release an Animal for the purpose of causing it to be impounded; or to fail
                  to reclaim an impounded Animal from an Animal Shelter, contracted with the City, after
                  having been notified that the Animal has been impounded. B. Adequate Care means normal care and prudent attention to the needs and welfare of an Animal, including
                  that care normally needed to maintain good health in a specific species of Animal,
                  including clean and dry bedding and resting surfaces, grooming, removal of manure,
                  and: 1. Adequate Food, which means wholesome foodstuffs suitable for the species provided at suitable intervals
                  in a Sanitary manner in quantities sufficient to maintain good health in an Animal
                  considering its age and condition; 2. Adequate Health Care, which means the provision to each healthy Animal of all immunizations and preventive
                  care required to maintain good health; space adequate to allow the Animal to rest
                  and exercise sufficient to maintain good health; and the provision to each sick, diseased
                  or injured Animal of necessary veterinary care or humane death; 3. Adequate Shelter, which means a structurally sound, properly ventilated, Sanitary and weatherproof
                  shelter suitable for the species, conditions and age of the Animal which provides
                  access to shade from direct sunlight…

questions.prompt: What do you need before holding a public meeting in a Wyandotte County park?
choices: A written permit from the director of parks
Verbal permission from any park attendant
Approval from the golf advisory board
Nothing, parks are always open for gatherings
questions.answer: A written permit from the director of parks
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Conduct within recreational facilities, § 22-4. State Law reference— Public recreation and playgrounds generally, K.S.A. 12-1901 et seq.

Editor's note— Ord. No. O-65-16 , § 1 adopted Nov. 17, 2016, repealed the former § 25-1, which pertained to mileage
               reimbursement and derived from Ord. No. O-98-06(Res. No. R-122-06), § 1, adopted Sept.
               21, 2006.

It shall be unlawful for any person to hold, conduct or engage in any public meeting
               in public parks and grounds within the city without first obtaining a written permit
               to do so from the director of parks. Such permit shall state the particular place
               and the hours between which such meeting shall be held. Such a permit shall be granted
               upon a showing that public safety or park property will not be endangered. (Code 1964, § 25-2; Code 1988, § 25-1) Cross reference— Parades, § 32-231 et seq.

The unified government may charge user fees for use of city park property and other
               city property under its jurisdiction, in amounts established by the county administrator. (Code 1964, § 25-6; Code 1988, § 25-2; Ord. No. 62638, § 1, 2-26-1981)

Footnotes: --- ( 2 ) --- Cross reference— Boards, commissions, etc., § 2-381 et seq.

There is created for the unified government a golf advisory board, in compliance with
               and to carry out the interlocal agreement entered into between the unified government
               and the City of Bonner Springs, Kansas, dated July 1, 1998. (Code 1988, § 25-21; Ord. No. O-42-98, § 1, 6-18-1998)

The golf advisory board shall be composed of 11 voting members and one nonvoting member.
               The nonvoting member shall, in an advisory capacity, be appointed to the golf advisory
               board by the governing body of the City of Bonner Springs, Kansas. (Code 1988, § 25-22; Ord. No. O-42-98, § 1, 6-18-1998)
